newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says tomato deal not a dumping admission.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says tomato deal not a dumping admission.

text.p: Mexico's government said Friday that the deal struck with the United States over the long-running tomato war is not an admission that Mexican growers dumped product in the neighboring country.
"The agreement to suspend (dumping investigations) does not imply the admission of dumping or damage to the U.S. (tomato) industry," the Trade Ministry said in a statement.
Both country's agreed Friduld not sell their produce in the United States at less than a so-called reference price of 20.68 cents per pound, or about $5.17 per 25-pound box.
Florida growers had claimed Mexicans were dumping product on the U.S. market at prices below cost or below Mexican prices, costing the U.S. industry hundreds of millions of dollars in lost sales.
"In the agreement, the Mexican tomato industry has guaranteed access of its products in the U.S. market, promising to sell them above a minimum price," the ministry said.
But Mexico reiterated its worry about the way in which U.S. authorities carried out the anti-dumping investigation.

"On several occasions, the government has made it clear that the investigation is incompatible with the codes established in the World Trade Organization and in the North American Free Trade Agreement," it added.
